teams.heading: Jake White to name final Fiji squad on Friday after Lyon camp
teams.body: Jake White will name Fiji's final Nations Championship squad on Friday, after a three-day Lyon camp to assess players. Kali Sewabu says White "wants to see and have a feel of everyone in the current squad" before deciding. Around 10 players from the 34-28 win over Japan flew straight to Europe, joining Europe-based names including Seta Bituniyata, the Pro D2 Player of the Year. Those players return to club games this weekend and regroup in Lyon, pending injuries.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item about the men's XV squad and selection, and it sets up the next team announcement.

teams.heading: Warren Gatland says Steve Borthwick has 'a lot at stake' this autumn
teams.body: Warren Gatland has put Steve Borthwick's job security in the spotlight ahead of the Northern Hemisphere leg of the Nations Championship. Speaking to BOYLE Sports, the former Wales and Lions coach said: "There's a lot at stake in terms of results. You lose and people lose their jobs." Gatland, who was on the 2017 Lions with Borthwick, praised his technical ability and said international coaching can take time to build. England's autumn opener is against Australia.

teams.heading: Gareth Anscombe explains Bayonne exit for Scarlets, citing wish to keep playing
teams.body: Gareth Anscombe, now 35, says he was weighing his options at the end of the Top 14 season with Bayonne when Scarlets' approach came late in the campaign. "I felt like I still had another year left in me," he said, adding that he did not really want to move his family too much. Dwayne Peel made the first contact, and Anscombe, who quit France for Wales, now plays in the URC for the Llanelli-based side.

teams.heading: Tadhg Furlong faces disciplinary hearing today after Gavin Coombes citation
teams.body: Tadhg Furlong faces a disciplinary committee today after being cited under Law 9.27 over Gavin Coombes' allegation that his groin was interfered with in the Leinster-Munster URC game. Leinster assistant Robin McBryde has defended the prop, saying "He's got no history of anything like that." Owen Doyle, a former head of Irish referees, argues any guilty verdict should be heavy enough to rule Furlong out of Ireland's November Tests, pointing to nine weeks for Jan-Hendrik Wessels in a similar case.

teams.heading: Tommaso Menoncello set to miss Italy's autumn Tests with shoulder sprain
teams.body: Toulouse centre Tommaso Menoncello is set to miss Italy's autumn campaign after suffering a sprained left shoulder when he went off in the 43rd minute of Sunday's 43-40 Champions Cup win over Exeter Chiefs. The injury is expected to keep him out for several weeks, another setback for the 24-year-old after an earlier knock against La Rochelle. Head coach Gonzalo Quesada must now prepare for the autumn without one of his key players, with South Africa, Argentina and Fiji on the calendar.

teams.heading: Finn Russell urges Scotland to kick on and beat big teams
teams.body: Finn Russell wants Scotland to kick on and beat the big teams, and he is in Gregor Townsend's 37-man squad for the Nations Championship. Scotland have yet to beat the All Blacks, who have won 31 of the 33 previous meetings, and the next test is at Murrayfield. Last time out they beat Fiji 33-17.

teams.heading: Gareth Anscombe says Dwayne Peel's approach lured him from Bayonne to Scarlets
teams.body: Gareth Anscombe says he left Bayonne for Scarlets because he felt he still had another year left in him, and that Dwayne Peel made the first approach. The 35-year-old, who won 42 caps for Wales, wanted to move back to Wales without moving the family too much, with his children about to start school. He played his second URC match for Scarlets in last weekend's 14-try thriller against the Stormers in Cape Town.

teams.heading: Santiago Carreras ruled out for rest of season with knee injury
teams.body: Santiago Carreras will miss the rest of the season after a serious knee injury suffered playing for Bath last weekend, Reuters reports, leaving Argentina without a utility back ahead of the Nations Championship. He limped off early in Bath's 23-5 defeat to Gloucester and is due a scan on the lower-limb injury. Mateo Soler, who made his test debut off the bench against Australia last month, has replaced him in the squad.

teams.heading: Les Kiss confirms Wallabies talks with Mark Nawaqanitawase over international future
teams.body: Les Kiss has spelled out where the Wallabies stand on Mark Nawaqanitawase, who has discussed his eligibility for Fiji and Italy. Speaking on the KOKO show before flying north for the November Nations Championship matches, the coach said Australia want the 26-year-old to know they are there to support him, but he must earn his jersey. Nawaqanitawase has won his maiden NRL title with the Sydney Roosters and joins Saitama Panasonic Wild Knights, so the three-way battle for his allegiance is live heading into Rugby World Cup 2027.

lead.why: Beale's recall was already led on Thursday, and Kiss's on-record comments on Nawaqanitawase are the freshest new item from a Wallabies source.

teams.heading: Jake White's first match in charge ends in 28-34 defeat to Fiji
teams.body: Jake White's first match in charge ended in a 28-34 defeat to Fiji at Prince Chichibunomiya, with Japan level 21-21 at half-time. White, who said he had not coached at international level for 20 years, reflected: "I'm very excited and relieved as we had a short time with this team." His stated priority is control, and the three Nations Championship fixtures against France, Ireland and Italy follow.

lead.why: The only men's XV item in the shortlist not already covered on this tab, and it gives a new angle on Japan's coaching change.

teams.heading: Anton Segner says two injuries have been tough mentally ahead of tour
teams.body: Rookie Anton Segner says the ankle and head injury assessment setbacks that have kept him out have been hard going. Speaking on the Aotearoa Rugby Pod ahead of the end-of-year tour to Scotland, Wales and England, the 25-year-old said "these last two injuries have really been tough on me mentally." Capped twice off the bench in July's wins over Italy and Ireland, the German-born back-rower said he is "looking forward to these next couple games and hoping to get some good game time."

lead.why: It is the strongest genuinely new item, a player speaking on his own setbacks, and it avoids the injury-list story already covered today.

teams.heading: Markus Muller's Test debut would make him youngest Springbok in professional era
teams.body: Markus Muller is poised to break a Springboks record if he makes his debut in the Nations Championship matches against Italy, France or Ireland. Planet Rugby reports he would become the youngest Springbok of the professional era, displacing Frans Steyn, who debuted at 19 years, 181 days under Jake White. Muller, who only turned 19 in July, started the key fixtures at the U20 World Championship and scored in the final win over France.
